title: Hyperkalemia — Emergency Management
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Hyperkalemia
Standard emergency-medicine / nephrology management; NEJM 2018 (bicarbonate in non-acidotic hyperkalemia)

changelog.change: Initial entry — the ECG-progression table, the stabilise → shift → eliminate ladder with doses and onset times, BRASH syndrome, and the bicarbonate / calcium-salt caveats.

summary: Treat empirically the moment there are ECG changes — do NOT wait for the repeat lab. K⁺ > 6.5 with ECG changes is immediately life-threatening. The sequence is STABILISE the membrane (calcium — buys 30–60 min, does NOT lower K⁺) → SHIFT K⁺ intracellularly (insulin + dextrose, albuterol) → ELIMINATE it (GI binder, diuresis, dialysis).

rows: PR prolongation, QRS widening (> 120 ms), P-wave flattening
Loss of P waves; sine-wave pattern; any rhythm; VF / asystole imminent

body.text: ECG changes correlate poorly with the absolute number — a normal ECG does not exclude dangerous hyperkalaemia, and any ECG change is an indication to give calcium NOW.

items: Calcium gluconate 1–3 g IV over 5–10 min (peripheral OK), OR calcium chloride 1 g IV via a CENTRAL line only. Onset 1–3 min, duration 30–60 min. Repeat q30 min if the ECG hasn't improved. Does NOT lower K⁺ — it only protects the myocardium.
Calcium chloride delivers 3× the elemental calcium per gram but causes severe tissue necrosis on extravasation — hence gluconate peripherally, chloride central.

rows: 10 units IV + D50W 50 mL (25 g dextrose). If BG > 250: omit the dextrose
Onset 15–30 min; lowers K⁺ 0.5–1.5 for 4–6 h. Monitor BG hourly — delayed hypoglycaemia is common (consider a D10 infusion)
10–20 mg (10–20× a standard 2.5 mg vial, stacked)
Onset ~30 min; lowers K⁺ 0.5–1.5; additive to insulin. Causes tachycardia — cautious use if arrhythmia-prone
ONLY effective in a metabolic acidosis — multiple RCTs / meta-analyses (incl. NEJM 2018) show minimal effect in non-acidotic patients. Not a routine agent
Patiromer 8.4 g PO, or sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g TID ×2 days — preferred over Kayexalate (SPS carries a rare but serious intestinal-necrosis risk, worse post-op / in ileus). Onset 2–7 h
Furosemide 40–80 mg IV — promotes renal K⁺ excretion; effective ONLY if urine output is present, useless in oliguric / anuric AKI. Give isotonic fluid alongside if volume-deplete
Emergent haemodialysis — definitive removal. Indicated for oliguric AKI, CKD stage 4–5, or K⁺ > 6.5 refractory to the above. Call nephrology immediately

body.text: BRASH syndrome: Bradycardia + Renal failure + AV block + Shock + Hyperkalaemia — bradycardia disproportionate to the K⁺ level and resistant to atropine, from synergy between AV-nodal agents (beta-blockers, diltiazem, verapamil) and hyperkalaemia. Treat the hyperkalaemia aggressively (calcium, insulin/dextrose, fluids ± dialysis) and treat the offending drug as a cofactor — this is not primary conduction disease.

buildNote: Tier 1 — a common, previously-missing emergency. Peds dosing (calcium gluconate 60–100 mg/kg, insulin 0.1 U/kg + 2 mL/kg D25, albuterol) is a natural companion in the Peds Module.
